text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests administered in a healthcare setting.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests administered in a healthcare setting

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood glucose level over the past 2 to 3 months.
Note: This test does not require fasting.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood glucose after you fast (nothing to eat or drink except water) for at least 8 hours.
Diabetes: 126 mg/dL or higher (7.0 mmol/L or higher)
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood glucose before and 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL or higher (11.1 mmol/L or higher) at the 2-hour mark
Prediabetes: 140 to 199 mg/dL (7.8 to 11.0 mmol/L) at the 2-hour mark
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood glucose at any time of day, regardless of when you last ate.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL or higher combined with classic diabetes symptoms (such as frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, or extreme thirst).
Repeating Tests: In most cases, if a test shows you are in the diabetes range without severe symptoms, your doctor will repeat the test on a separate day to confirm the diagnosis.
Over-the-Counter Meters: Home finger-prick blood glucose meters are used to monitor levels, but cannot be used to diagnose diabetes.
You can learn more about testing procedures via the MedlinePlus Diabetes Type 2 Guide or review official criteria through the American Diabetes Association Diagnosis Page.
